svg.title: RIEMANN R8 — Galois representations: every statement of the chapter, and what each one rests on
svg.desc: The blueprint's chapter 8 in one poster: its 38 statements as cards, each with the Lean declaration it stands for, the statement in words, how its proof goes, and what it uses and is used by. Read it from the foot up: the chapter's theorem, thm-galois-reps-polarized, is at the bottom, and every card stands above the cards whose proofs use it. An arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A; a dashed arrow says that the proof of B names A without listing it as a use. The statements that head a section or a group of results have full cards; the others are drawn shorter. The chapter's own introduction: This chapter proves thm-galois-reps-polarized: every polarized regular algebraic cuspidal representation π of GL_a over a CM field has an l-adic Galois representation, with the Hodge–Tate weights read off π and with Weil–Deligne representations that match the local parameters of π wherever these are determined (rem-local-parameters-weak). The outline needs it in thm-grh-from-galois: these representations bound the Tate–Shafarevich groups of chap-sha and enter the families of chap-families. The statement is a weak form of the theorem of Harris–Taylor, Shin, Chenevier–Harris, Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor and Caraiani. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.

text.tspan: 2 · The chapter, from its leaves down to its theorem

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 14 rows. Section by section the chapter runs: 1. From odd rank and theta lifts to all polarized pairs (3); 2. Local-global compatibility at ramified places (3); 3. Geometric Galois representations in odd rank (2); 4. Hecke eigenspaces in etale cohomology (9); 5. Kuga-Sato varieties over unitary Shimura varieties (4); 6. Integral models of compact unitary Shimura varieties (7); 7. Base change between definite unitary groups and GL(n) (7); 8. The forms used by the families (2). The cards keep

svg.text: In the situation of thm-unitary-shimura-integral-models, the moduli problem is

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: represented by an R-scheme X with a universal object, and X is quasi-projective over R. The

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: proof uses Mumford's geometric invariant theory.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: subquotient ρ of G_E, and every graded piece of a G_E-stable filtration of V_θ qualifies.

text.tspan: 1. From odd rank and theta lifts to all polarized pairs

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: This section reduces thm-galois-reps-polarized to two inputs (

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: sec-gal-odd-rank and the non-vanishing of theta lifts from definite unitary groups (

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: thm-theta-lift-nonvanishing, after Rallis and Li). From the odd-rank representations

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: we cut out a piece of the right dimension, reach all weights by congruences and a limit,

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: in the style of Chenevier, of pseudo-representations, isolate even-rank representations

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: between two theta lifts to odd rank, and descend from GL_a to unitary groups. The

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: ramified places are left to sec-gal-ramified.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: sec-gal-assembly gives Galois representations compatible at the unramified places;

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: this section adds the ramified places that def-galois-reps-polarized asks about (

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: thm-local-global-ramified). Compatibility first extends to principal series from

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: characters no two of which differ by |·|. At a depth-zero place over Q_g, a solvable base

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: change makes the component a principal series of that kind (

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: thm-depth-zero-base-change-principal-series), and restricting to the smaller Galois

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: group does not change inertia. Where the definition asks only for the dimension of the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Weil–Deligne representation, there is nothing to prove.

text.tspan: 3. Geometric Galois representations in odd rank

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: This section supplies the first input of sec-gal-assembly. We move an automorphic

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: representation of the definite unitary group U_a, a odd, with a cuspidal type at one place

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: above l and lacunary weights at another, to a Hecke eigensystem on a compact unitary

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Shimura variety of signature (1, a-1) (thm-transfer-unitary-shimura). The

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Kuga–Sato varieties over it (sec-gal-kuga-sato) and the results on Hecke eigenspaces (

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: sec-gal-eigenspaces) give a Galois representation of unknown dimension on which the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: This section is general étale cohomology, with no unitary groups. For a smooth

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: projective variety with finite étale Hecke correspondences, each system of Hecke

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: eigenvalues cuts out a Galois representation on cohomology (

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: thm-galois-reps-hecke-eigenspaces). A congruence relation at a place of good

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: reduction controls Frobenius; a good model above l makes the representation

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: crystalline; and the Hodge–Tate decomposition, which commutes with the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: correspondences, gives Hodge–Tate weights from Hodge numbers. The classical inputs

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: (proper base change, the projective bundle formula, finiteness) come first.

text.tspan: 5. Kuga-Sato varieties over unitary Shimura varieties

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: This section shows that the Kuga–Sato varieties over compact unitary Shimura varieties

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: of signature (1, n-1), the fibre powers of the universal abelian scheme, satisfy the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: thm-kuga-sato-unitary-shimura). Their smoothness and good reduction come from

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: the integral models of sec-gal-shimura-models. The Hodge numbers of their

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: eigenspaces come from the holomorphic Lefschetz formula: fixed points of Hecke

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: correspondences are CM points, and the sum over them is a sum of orbital integrals.

svg.text: The Kuga–Sato varieties of sec-gal-kuga-sato live over integral models of unitary

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Shimura varieties of Harris–Taylor type. This section proves, after Kottwitz, that the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: moduli problem is represented by a quasi-projective scheme, smooth of relative

svg.text: base change. This section states weak base change in isobaric form (

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: thm-base-change-unitary, after Labesse) and in the form with local components (

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: thm-labesse-base-change). It also gives the local results behind the comparison of

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: trace formulas: a bound for Hecke operators, from wave kernels on GL_n(ℂ) and the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma; a twisted trace on the lowest type at the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: archimedean places; and the Leibniz rule for Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivatives.
